text:
samir: Heads-up — I'm putting together a lightweight 'handshake' contract for control-plane <-> runtime that should cover Hosted, Dedicated, and Private without leaking hosted-only knobs. Want to keep surface minimal so on-prem teams can implement quickly.

alex: sounds good. can you paste the current sketch?

samir: sure, rough proto sketch below — meant to be machine-negotiated at registration time:```json
{
  "runtime_id": "string",
  "protocol_version": "1.0",
  "capabilities": ["generation", "streaming", "kv_cache"],
  "observability_labels": {"region": "string", "hardware_class": "string"},
  "slo_tier": "gold|silver|bronze",
  "fallbacks": ["model:v1", "model:v0-quant"],
  "security": {"kms": "managed|customer|none"},
  "accepts_canary": true
}
```

maria: nice. major concern: if we hide model variant details behind the runtime we lose per-model cost/latency telemetry. can we require a "telemetry_map" label that maps model identifiers to observable keys?

dinesh: also need a place to express reserved capacity hints. Dedicated will want to expose something like `capacity_reservation: {units:int, min_qps:int}` so scheduler can respect it.

jin: and rollouts — control plane must be able to ask runtime whether it supports canaries and atomic swaps. accepts_canary is ok, but what about an `apply_rollout(token)` handshake so runtime can validate a rollout request?

samir: good points. my intent was minimal, but we can add optional sections. suggestion: keep required core fields (id, version, capabilities) and make telemetry/slo/security/fallbacks optional structured annotations. makes it easier for private installs to return a "lite" object.

alex: +1. from an API perspective I'd prefer capabilities be expressive tags rather than booleans. e.g. `capabilities: ["streaming:v2", "kv_cache:shared"]` so we can extend without bumping major.

maria: also require a `observability_labels.owner` and `observability_labels.model_key` convention so billing/quality teams can map tokens back to model tenants. we shouldn't invent freeform keys that every customer implements differently.

dinesh: ephemeral edge case: what if runtime doesn't support streaming? we need an enum `streaming_mode: none|chunked|server_sent_events` so control plane can fallback to poll-mode gracefully.

samir: agreed. i'll fold those into the RFC. action items: samir -> update RFC with the contract sketch + compatibility table for older runtimes; alex -> add examples for capability tagging; maria -> propose strict observability label set; dinesh -> spec capacity_reservation shape; jin -> sketch a rollout validation handshake.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot posted: RFC 2067894321-handshake-proposal.md has been created in #architecture (link: https://redwood/repo/rfcs/2067894321) :rocket:

alex: quick question — how do we handle stable vs experimental fields? e.g. `accepts_canary` might be experimental. we need a `field_stability` map or versioned protocol negotiation.

samir: plan: protocol_version is the ground truth. optional `experimental` capability tags allowed but control plane must not route production traffic to runtimes advertising experimental-only flags unless customer opts in. we'll document the safety rules.

maria: one more — for Private, customers may require the handshake to be transmitted over mTLS and a signed attestation blob. add `attestation: {type, signature}` optional.

dinesh: thanks. once we agree I'll also add unit tests for the scheduler that simulate runtimes returning partial/older handshake objects. catches compatibility bugs early.

jin: LGTM. can we have a short example of a minimal private handshake and a full hosted handshake in the RFC? that will help implementers.

samir: yup i'll add both. will ping when updated. :thumbsup:

alex: :eyes:

maria: :+1:

dinesh: thanks all — this clears up the main tradeoffs.

samir: closing loop: aim to merge RFC by Friday so eng teams can start shims next week.
